To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition to mothering shifts the average frequency tuning of inhibitory neurons in the auditory cortex, and that this shift is accompanied by a reduction in inhibition and an increase in excitation.
the transition to mothering shifts the average best-frequency tuning of PVNs in the auditory cortex to higher frequencies and reduces the inhibitory response to pup odors.

(i) maternal odor exposure induces plasticity in the frequency tuning of PVNs, (ii) maternal odor exposure reduces PVN activity, (iii) maternal odor exposure increases PyrN activity, and (iv) maternal odor exposure enhances responses of PyrN to pup vocalizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of motherhood on neural processing of auditory information in the primary auditory cortex.
the plasticity of the auditory cortex in mother mice.
the role of sensory processing during motherhood, and the mechanisms underlying plasticity in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the plasticity of the auditory cortex during motherhood is driven by the presence of pup odours and results in a selective shift in the frequency tuning of the PVN and a complementary increase in spontaneous and stimulus-driven activity of PyrN.
the transition to mothering induces a shift in the frequency tuning of PVNs, and that this shift is accompanied by a selective reduction of pup-odor-evoked activity in PVNs.
maternal behavior changes the frequency tuning of PVNs, and that this shift in frequency tuning results in a reduction of feedforward inhibitory input to PyrNs in L2/3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transition to mother hood shifts the excitability balance of the auditory cortex towards increased responsiveness to ultrasonic vocalization, the most important form of communication between mother and pup.
the transition to mother hood is associated with a plasticity of the inhibitory circuitry of the auditory cortex, that is likely to be involved in the processing of pup vocalizations.

the transition to mother hood shifts the frequency tuning of PVN to a higher frequency, and this shift in PVN frequency tuning is likely to be a result of the reduction of feedforward inhibitions from PVN to L2/3 PyrNs, and this reduction of inhibitions is likely to be mediated by a reduction in the spontaneous activity of PVN
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transition to mother hood is accompanied by a shift of the frequency tuning of PVNs in the primary auditory cortex and a concomitant reduction in feedforward inhibition.
the transition to mother hood is accompanied by changes in the response properties of inhibitory neurons, with a shift in frequency tuning and reduced activity in response to pup odorants.
the transition to mothering can induce plasticity in the brain, and that the plasticity is mediated by the sensory cues from the pups.
